title: Compact Shift Digest: Contextual Alert Summaries & Postmortem Shortcuts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: On-call engineers and incident owners need a lightweight summary view they can skim at shift handoffs. Current incident tiles in the console are too verbose, require multiple clicks to reach runbooks/postmortems, and do not surface SLO delta context alongside cost/latency trends. Goal: Design a compact 'Shift Digest' card that surfaces the top 3 active alerts, an SLO delta sparkline, quick actions (acknowledge, escalate, snooze), and a one-click Postmortem/Runbook shortcut. The digest should fit in a single-line card for lists and expand into a contextual drawer without losing keyboard focus. Key UX properties: - density: compact by default; expanded drawer for deep actions - contextual linking: direct link to latest postmortem for an alert when available - SLO delta: small sparkline with hover tooltip for 1h/6h/24h - cost awareness: optional token showing recent cost delta for the service - privacy: redact sensitive incident metadata in shift exports - keyboard-first: first-class quick actions via single-key hotkeys - performance constraint: avoid loading full postmortem or heavy SLO queries on list render (use cached payloads and lazy fetch)
acceptance_criteria: Compact Shift Digest card shows up to 3 top alerts with severity badges and short summaries (<=80 chars)
Each alert row has an inline SLO delta sparkline and a one-click Postmortem shortcut when a postmortem exists
Card supports three states: collapsed (single line), expanded (drawer), and pinned (persisted for the shift)
Quick actions (Acknowledge/Escalate/Snooze) available from collapsed state via kebab menu or keyboard hotkeys
Design includes microcopy for privacy mode and export behavior; meets AA color contrast for badges and actions
Prototype demonstrates lazy-loading of full postmortem content and uses placeholder skeletons while loading
Hand-off flows include links to the canonical postmortem doc, related GitHub PRs, and the incident timeline URL
Engineering design notes include caching strategy and fallback behavior if SLO query times out
decisions: Show up to 3 alerts to keep card height consistent; further alerts accessible in expanded drawer
Use sparklines for SLO deltas instead of numeric-only deltas to give trend context at a glance
Expose postmortem shortcut only when a linked postmortem exists; otherwise show 'File postmortem' CTA
Avoid preloading full postmortem bodies on list render to reduce load; use cached metadata and lazy fetch on expand
Built-in keyboard shortcuts (A = acknowledge, E = escalate, S = snooze) to reduce mouse travel during handoff
Cost token is hidden behind a toggle to reduce noise for teams that don’t track cost during incidents
